audit.primary_source_citation: Gamliel M, Goldman-Wohl D, Isaacson B, Gur C, Stein N, Yamin R, Berger M, Grunewald M, Keshet E, Rais Y, Bornstein C, David E, Jelinski A, Eisenberg I, Greenfield C, Ben-David A, Imbar T, Gilad R, Haimov-Kochman R, Mankuta D, Elami-Suzin M, Amit I, Hanna JH, Yagel S, Mandelboim O. "Trained Memory of Human Uterine NK Cells Enhances Their Function in Subsequent Pregnancies." Immunity 2018;48(5):951-962.e5. DOI 10.1016/j.immuni.2018.03.030. PMID 29768178. Associated primary data: GEO GSE79879 (RNA-seq, 2 libraries) and GSE100636 (ATAC-seq, 6 libraries). NOTE: the hint's citation is correct as a citation but MISDESCRIBES the paper — "PTdNK" in Gamliel means "Pregnancy Trained decidual NK", NOT "postpartum decidual NK", and the paper contains no postpartum sample of any kind.
audit.fulltext_unavailable_reason: Immunity is not open access; Europe PMC/PubMed returned ABSTRACT_ONLY and cell.com/sciencedirect returned HTTP 403 to direct fetch. Complete main text + STAR Methods were obtained via a reader proxy and read in full (archived at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-aaa/5f46e874-56b9-5c6b-9d27-d08dbfb1d5d8/scratchpad/gamliel_jina.txt). Supplementary Tables S1-S10 (mmc1.pdf), which carry the per-figure donor counts and epidemiological data, could NOT be retrieved (HTTP 422). Per-donor n for the flow-cytometry figures therefore comes only from the numbers stated in the main text and from GEO sample metadata, which I retrieved in full for both accessions.
audit.species: Human (primary evidence: first-trimester decidua and menstrual-blood-derived endometrial NK cells). Mouse (C57BL/6-Tg Act-EGFP aortic rings ex vivo; SCID-Beige females, 5-6 per group, JEG3 xenograft) used ONLY as bioassays for VEGFa activity in human dNK supernatants — no mouse experiment bears on persistence or ancestry.
audit.what_was_measured: In humans, all HCMV-seropositive, a SINGLE cross-sectional measurement per woman was taken: (a) in first-trimester (6-14 wk gestation) decidua obtained at elective termination, flow cytometry measured %NKG2C-hi among CD56bright CD3- dNK and LILRB1 MFI on NKG2C-hi vs NKG2C-neg dNK, comparing primigravid to multigravid donors; (b) in menstrual blood collected on cycle days 1-2 from separate NON-PREGNANT women (nulligravid vs women who had given birth within the past 5 years), the same two flow readouts were measured on endometrial NK cells; (c) bulk RNA-seq compared sorted NKG2C-hi vs NKG2C-neg dNK as ONE library each, from 5 multigravid deciduas pooled before sorting; (d) bulk ATAC-seq compared NKG2C-hi dNK (primigravid vs multigravid) and NKG2C-hi eNK (nulligravid vs multigravid) as ONE library per group, from pooled donors (4 primigravid and 7 multigravid deciduas); (e) IFN-g and VEGFa were measured by ELISA/intracellular stain after 48-72 h co-culture of purified dNK with irradiated 721.221, 721.221-HLA-E or 721.221-HLA-G transfectants plus rhIL-15, with anti-CD94 and anti-LILRB1 blockade. No woman was sampled at more than one timepoint; no first-pregnancy and subsequent-pregnancy sample came from the same individual; no postpartum uterine tissue, decidua or endometrium was sampled at any point.
audit.n: Flow-cytometry cohort sizes per figure live in Tables S1-S9, which I could not retrieve. Numbers stated in the main text / GEO: RNA-seq = 5 multigravid decidual donors POOLED into 1 sample, yielding 1 NKG2C-hi and 1 NKG2C-neg library (GSM2107769/70), no biological replicates, cuffdiff run on n=1 vs n=1; qRT-PCR validation on a second independent pool; LILRB1 MFI quantified on 8 multigravid decidua samples; decidual ATAC-seq = 4 primigravid donors pooled and 7 multigravid donors pooled, 1 library per group (GSM3030146/47), plus 1 pooled multigravid NKG2C-hi and 1 pooled NKG2C-neg library from 3 multigravid deciduas (GSM2689786/87); endometrial ATAC-seq = 1 pooled nulligravid and 1 pooled multigravid library (GSM3030144/45); Nuvaring subgroup = 3 nulligravid women; mouse xenograft = 5-6 mice/group; aortic rings = 6 rings/condition. GEO states explicitly for the decisive first-vs-subsequent-pregnancy ATAC comparison: "Tissue from sample GSM3030146 (positive_primigravidae_dNK) is from a different individual than sample GSM3030147 (positive_multigravidae_subsequent_pregnancy_dNK)."
audit.n_unit: women (donors) for flow cytometry; for RNA-seq and ATAC-seq the effective statistical n is 1 SEQUENCING LIBRARY per group with multiple donors pooled before library prep, so donor-level variance is unestimable. Mouse assays are per animal (5-6/group) or per aortic ring (6/condition). No cell-level counts were used as n here.
audit.controls: PRESENT: analysis restricted to HCMV-seropositive women (ImmunoComb II CMV IgG), explicitly to pre-empt the HCMV-adaptive-NK confound; matched isotype controls for every stain and sort; internal cell-type control (NKG2C on decidual T cells from the same women — no primigravid/multigravid difference); internal subset control (NKG2C-neg dNK from the same pooled sample as the NKG2C-hi RNA-seq/ATAC library); reported non-correlation of %NKG2C-hi with gestational week (Fig 1E) and with maternal age (Fig 1F); a gravidity>=2 / parity 0 subgroup (Fig 1G); parental 721.221 vs HLA-E and HLA-G transfectants, anti-CD94 and anti-LILRB1 blockade, and anti-VEGF (bevacizumab) blockade for the functional assays; exclusion of hormonal contraceptive users from the main menstrual cohort with Nuvaring users analysed separately. ABSENT AND MATERIAL: no age matching — primigravid donors averaged 22 y (18-27) and multigravid 34 y (24-45), a ~12 y gap in the exact axis along which HCMV-driven NKG2C-hi expansion accumulates; no CMV-seronegative comparison arm; no biological replicates for RNA-seq or ATAC-seq (n=1 library per group, donors pooled, so donor identity, HLA/KIR genotype and batch are perfectly confounded with group); no same-woman longitudinal sampling; no postpartum sample; no clonality, KIR-repertoire-clonality, barcoding, somatic-variant or fate-mapping assay of any kind; Student's t test applied uniformly, including to bounded proportion data.
audit.strongest_alternative_explanation: Four alternatives, each individually sufficient, none excluded by the design. (1) AGE / CUMULATIVE HCMV EXPOSURE CONFOUND: the multigravid group is ~12 years older than the primigravid group (mean 34 vs 22). NKG2C-hi expansion is the canonical HCMV imprint and keeps accumulating with age and with duration of HCMV carriage even among seropositives, so restricting to HCMV-seropositive women controls serostatus but not exposure duration or reactivation history. The entire Figure 1 effect (2.93% vs 17.0%) is reproducible by age alone with zero pregnancy memory. (2) THE PAPER'S OWN NUVARING DATA REFUTE PREGNANCY-SPECIFICITY: 3 NEVER-PREGNANT women using an estradiol vaginal ring had endometrial NKG2C-hi frequencies "far greater than the nulligravid samples". A hormonal exposure with zero pregnancies reproduces the marker, so NKG2C-hi tracks steroid/uterine microenvironment conditioning, not a surviving pregnancy-experienced clone. (3) RECRUITMENT AND RE-DIFFERENTIATION INSTEAD OF PERSISTENCE: Strunz et al., Sci Immunol 2021 (PMID 33617461) show, using human uterus transplant recipients and monozygotic twins, that the uNK niche is replenished from the circulation and that uNK phenotype is under genetic control. A parous-vs-nulliparous phenotype difference therefore arises equally well from ongoing recruitment of blood NK into a differently conditioned uterus, with no cell surviving from the previous pregnancy. (4) POOLING ARTEFACT IN THE "EPIGENETIC SIGNATURE": with 1 ATAC library per group and donors pooled, every peak difference is confounded with donor identity and batch; and the authors themselves report that the IFNG and VEGFA enhancers — the mechanistic core of the memory model — "did not differ in genomic accessibility between the NKG2C-hi samples", i.e. the epigenetic mark that is supposed to be carried forward is precisely the one that fails to distinguish the populations. Additionally, the direction of the claimed arrow is wrong: the authors' own conclusion is that PTdNK PRECURSORS sit in the endometrium between pregnancies and are CONVERTED during the next pregnancy — and their attempt to perform that conversion in vitro on blood or endometrial NK failed ("Such conversion was unsuccessful").
audit.counter_evidence: FOUND, and it targets exactly the load-bearing figure. Feyaerts D, van der Meer A, Joosten I, van der Molen RG. "Selective expansion and CMV-dependency in pregnancy trained human endometrial NK cells." Cell Mol Immunol 2019;16(4):410-411. PMID 30635647 / PMC6462002 (full text read). Independent endometrial cohort: n=10 nulligravidae vs n=25 multigravidae, CMV serology in 24 (11 pos, 13 neg, 11 not determined). Verbatim: "we did not see an increase in the percentage of NKG2C+ endometrial NK (eNK) cells and the percentage of LILRB1 expression on NKG2C+ eNK cells in multigravidae compared to nulligravidae women, irrespective of CMV status." Only a non-significant "trend" in LILRB1 on NKG2C+ eNK survived in the CMV-positive subgroup, and even there "no difference in the percentage of NKG2C+ eNK cells was observed when comparing nulli- and multigravidae CMV pos samples." This is a direct failure to replicate Gamliel Figure 5C-5D, which IS the between-pregnancy persistence evidence, in a cohort larger than Gamliel's. Feyaerts' one positive finding — self-HLA-C-specific KIR subpopulation expansions in 5/25 multigravid endometria, present in both CMV-pos and CMV-neg donors — is the closest thing in this literature to a clonality observation, it comes from the CONTRADICTING paper rather than from Gamliel, and it is itself an outlier analysis on flow data (still INF_MARKER). Also relevant: Feyaerts et al., Front Immunol 2024 (PMID 38571943) profiled eNK vs dNK receptor repertoires and attributed the differences to pregnancy state rather than to gravidity-linked persistence; Strunz et al., Sci Immunol 2021 (PMID 33617461) supplies the replenishment-from-circulation alternative. SEPARATELY AND EXPLICITLY: I searched for any human study sampling POSTPARTUM uterine tissue (decidua or endometrium) to test whether pregnancy-associated NK cells persist after delivery, and found none — this is "searched and not found", not "does not exist" (G3).

audit.audit_overturns_detail: Claude's initial call was "QUASI-CLONAL (Gamliel 2018, NKG2C-high, ATAC)". Every element of that call fails on the methods. (1) NO CLONALITY WAS MEASURED. There is no clonality assay anywhere in the paper — no KIR-repertoire clonality analysis, no barcoding, no somatic-variant or mtDNA lineage tracing, no fate mapping. "Quasi-clonal" is not a weakened version of a clonality result; it is an unsupported import from the peripheral-blood HCMV-adaptive-NK literature. The paper in fact reports that PTdNK LACK the canonical adaptive signature: they do not express CD57 or DNAM-1 and they retain FceRIg, NKp30 and NKp46, and the authors conclude PTdNK are "characterized by increased expression of LILRB1 and NKG2C, and not by other memory related receptors." (2) THE ATAC CANNOT CARRY THE CALL. GSE100636 is 1 library per group with donors pooled and no replicates, and GEO's own annotation states that the primigravid and multigravid decidual NKG2C-hi libraries are "from a different individual" — so the first-vs-subsequent-pregnancy epigenetic comparison is a one-donor-pool-versus-another-donor-pool contrast, not a within-lineage measurement. The RNA-seq (GSE79879) is likewise 1 vs 1, cuffdiff on 5 pooled multigravid deciduas. And the IFNG/VEGFA enhancer accessibility — the supposed memory mark — did not differ between the NKG2C-hi samples. (3) PERSISTENCE WAS INFERRED, NEVER OBSERVED. Every comparison is between DIFFERENT WOMEN sampled ONCE. No woman was sampled in a first and then a subsequent pregnancy. (4) THE CLAIM'S OWN WORDING IS WRONG ABOUT THE SOURCE. PTdNK stands for "Pregnancy Trained decidual NK cells", not "postpartum decidual NK cells". The paper contains no postpartum sample; the closest proxy is menstrual-blood NK from non-pregnant women who had delivered within 5 years, compared against never-pregnant women. Worse for the "after delivery" framing, the NKG2C-hi expansion was seen in women with gravidity>=2 and PARITY ZERO — i.e. it tracks having been pregnant, not having delivered, so "persisting after delivery" is contradicted by the source's own Figure 1G. (5) The authors' proposed arrow is the opposite of the claim's: endometrial precursor -> PTdNK during the NEXT pregnancy, and their in vitro attempt to drive that conversion failed. Corrected classification: INF_MARKER (cross-sectional marker frequency across different women), the weakest observational-looking class that fits, with INF_INVITRO and INF_KINETIC also present and no OBS_* class of any kind.
audit.methods_quote: STAR Methods, Experimental Model and Subject Details: "Deciduae were obtained from elective first trimester (6-14 weeks) termination of normal pregnancies. Average age of the women was 22 for primigravid women (range 18-27), and 34 for multigravid women (24-45)." // "Blood was taken from healthy, HCMV positive female donors (age 20-43), who had given birth in the past 5 years." // ATAC methods: "NKG2C hi dNK cells purified from pooled decidua samples (4 for primigravid and 7 for multigravid) were sorted... The same was done with pooled nulligravid and multigravid endometrial NKG2C hi cells." // RNA-seq methods: "Five different multigravid decidual samples were treated as described above for lymphocyte separation and then pooled." // Results (the mechanistic core failing): "The IFNG and VEGFA enhancers, shown to differ between the NKG2C hi and NKG2C neg of multigravid dNK cells (Figure 3A), did not differ in genomic accessibility between the NKG2C hi samples." // Results (conversion failed): "To test whether we could convert peripheral blood or endometrial NK cells into PTdNKs, we initially incubated these cells with cells expressing HLA-G and HLA-E under various conditions. Such conversion was unsuccessful." // Results (pregnancy-specificity broken by hormone exposure alone): "Three women with gravidity zero... who reported use of a locally hormonal contraceptive named Nuvaring (an estradiol vaginal ring)... increased percentages of NKG2C hi cells were found among the endometrial NK cells obtained from these women, which was far greater than the nulligravid samples." // Results (tracks gravidity, not delivery): "the NKG2C hi expansion was observed even if previous pregnancies did not reach term; i.e., gravidity>=2, parity zero." // Statistics, in full: "Data are represented as mean +/- standard deviation (s.d.). Statistical significance was uniformly set at a minimum of P< 0.05 using Student's t test." // GEO GSM3030146/GSM3030147 sample annotation, verbatim: "Tissue from sample GSM3030146 (positive_primigravidae_dNK) is from a different individual than sample GSM3030147 (positive_multigravidae_subsequent_pregnancy_dNK)."
audit.notes: IS THIS A LINEAGE CLAIM? Yes — plainly. R4 as registered ("dNK -> PTdNK (postpartum persistence)") asserts identity of cells across time: that the decidual NK population present during a pregnancy is the same population (or its progeny) present afterwards. That is an ancestry/persistence assertion, "does A give rise to / remain as B", not a functional-restoration assertion. It is therefore NOT of the same kind as R1 (dNK -> cytotoxic under IL-15/IL-18, "can A's function be restored") or R3 (TGF-beta withdrawal). It sits in the registry's "reversal" group but is not a reversibility claim at all — it is a persistence claim, and the group label is a category error worth flagging for the later phase. TWO SEPARATE THINGS ARE CONFLATED IN THE CLAIM. (a) A lineage/persistence proposition: the same cells persist. Nothing in the primary source measures this. (b) A functional/state proposition: dNK from women in a repeated pregnancy secrete more IFN-gamma and VEGFalpha on NKG2C/LILRB1 engagement. This IS measured, in vitro, with blocking controls, and is the paper's real result. The lineage half is what R4 asserts and what has no evidence; the functional half has evidence and is not what R4 asserts. THE CITATION IS MISREMEMBERED IN A WAY THAT MATTERS. PTdNK = "Pregnancy Trained decidual NK", not "postpartum decidual NK". Gamliel 2018 sampled first-trimester decidua at elective termination and menstrual blood from non-pregnant women. It never sampled postpartum uterine tissue. The word "postpartum" in R4 has no referent in the cited source, and the source's Figure 1G (expansion present at gravidity>=2 with parity zero) affirmatively decouples the phenotype from delivery. I could not locate ANY human study that sampled postpartum uterus to test persistence; recorded as searched-and-not-found. WHAT THE ATAC ACTUALLY ESTABLISHES: that one pool of NKG2C-hi cells from some women has a different accessibility profile from another pool from other women, at n=1 library per group, with the two enhancers central to the memory model showing no difference between them. It establishes nothing about persistence or clonal descent. RECOMMENDED ROW-LEVEL VERDICT for later phases: the persistence/ancestry half of R4 is unevidenced and has a direct published non-replication (Feyaerts 2019) of its only human anchor; the functional half is real but is a different claim. I make no judgement about whether the underlying biology is worth pursuing.
